rationale: Sections 2.1–2.3 and Fig. 3: the network supplies a constitutive law; the design updates use adjoint sensitivities and MMA, with no learned optimizer compared against a classical optimizer.

Sections 3–4 and conclusion: the network predicts lattice material properties inside a gradient-based topology optimizer; comparisons assess optimized designs, not a learned optimization method against classical optimization.

Section 4.2, Table 3: the neural-network-based data-driven optimization is compared with constitutive-model-based topology optimization on final compliance; the reported differences are under 3%, without a primary speed comparison.
Methods, Eqs. 23–31, and Fig. 3: parametrized quantum circuits solve equilibrium and search over structures, but the article does not use a learned model for topology optimization.
Section 4, computational-cost comparison: conventional FE² requires 2,646 minutes per cantilever iteration and an estimated 551 days for 300 iterations; the neural surrogate design took 300 minutes.

Abstract: the learned latent geometry guides lattice optimization, while a classical topology-optimization comparison is suggested but no comparable outcome is stated; the full article was unavailable.
Section 4.2, Table 5: the VAE latent-space optimizer benchmarks final compliance against published classical multi-material topology optimizers, finding results within 5% of those methods.
Section 7.1, Table 1: neural-network-based multiscale optimization is compared with single-scale classical topology optimization on final compliance under the same nominal stiff-material constraint.
Abstract: gamma-ray shielding topology is optimized with an analytical attenuation model; machine learning appears only as background, and the publisher full text requires payment.
Abstract: the proposed topology optimizer designs ferromagnetic composites for magnetic actuators, an electromagnetic application outside the protocol's physics scope; full text was not reachable.
Abstract: a neural network converts users' sketches into topology-optimization variables, but the stated numerical examples do not establish a classical-method comparison; full text is paywalled.
SSRN abstract and protocol §11: this is an SSRN-only preprint, whereas eligible preprints must be on arXiv; the linked full-text PDF returned access denied.
Title page and results, Table 2: this is an Engineering Archive preprint without an arXiv version, a preprint type excluded by protocol §11.
Section 3, Eq. 21: only the cross-sectional areas of a fixed truss are optimized; neither its member connectivity nor material topology is redesigned.
Section 2: the neural network parameterizes cross-sectional areas in a fixed truss for weight minimization, which is member sizing rather than topology optimization.
Abstract: the method solves general neural-network objective optimization and an additive-manufacturing fatigue example; no topology or architected-material inverse-design problem is described.
Abstract: the density field is represented with a truncated Fourier basis and optimized classically; no learned model is used, and publisher full text is paywalled.
